finding: Al-Tabari's direct preferred interpretation reads the command as devotion of prayer and sacrificial worship to God alone, in gratitude for al-Kawthar, in contrast with worshipping others and sacrificing to idols. The final interpretive gloss follows the stated rationale; it is not a report route.

claim.statement_en: Tabari's preferred interpretation directs prayer and sacrificial worship to God alone in gratitude for al-Kawthar, contrasting this with worship of others and sacrifice to idols.
claim.controlled_translation_proposal: Of these views, the soundest in my judgment is the view that this means: Make all your prayer sincerely for your Lord alone, apart from rivals and gods; likewise make your sacrifice for Him, apart from idols, in gratitude for the honor and good He granted you by giving you al-Kawthar. I consider this view soundest because God informed His Prophet of His favor in granting al-Kawthar and then commanded him to pray and sacrifice; the command thus directs both acts to Him in gratitude for that blessing. The final gloss is: We have granted you al-Kawthar as favor and honor, so devote worship to your Lord and direct prayer and ritual sacrifice to Him alone, unlike those who disbelieve, worship another, and sacrifice to idols.
